nodes.summary: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo 4 and, for a natural number $n$, write $S(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} \chi_4(d)$ for the sum over the positive divisors $d$ of $n$ (so $S(0) = 0$). If $m$ and $n$ are coprime natural numbers, then $S(mn) = S(m)\,S(n)$.
nodes.title: The divisor sum of $\chi_4$ is multiplicative

nodes.summary: For the nonprincipal Dirichlet character $\chi_4$ modulo 4, the sum $\sum_{d \mid 1} \chi_4(d)$ over the divisors of $1$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: The divisor sum of $\chi_4$ at one

nodes.summary: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo 4. If $q$ is a prime with $q \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and $f$ is a natural number, then $\sum_{d \mid q^f} \chi_4(d)$ equals $1$ when $f$ is even and $0$ when $f$ is odd.
nodes.title: The divisor sum of $\chi_4$ at powers of a prime $q \equiv 3 \pmod 4$

nodes.summary: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo 4. If $p$ is a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and $e$ is a natural number, then $\sum_{d \mid p^e} \chi_4(d) = e + 1$.
nodes.title: The divisor sum of $\chi_4$ at powers of a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$

nodes.summary: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo 4. For every natural number $e$, $\sum_{d \mid 2^e} \chi_4(d) = 1$: only the divisor $1$ contributes.
nodes.title: The divisor sum of $\chi_4$ at powers of two

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the integer $\sum_{d \mid n} \chi_4(d)$, the sum over the positive divisors $d$ of $n$ of the nonprincipal Dirichlet character $\chi_4$ modulo 4, which takes the value $0$ at even $d$, $1$ at $d \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and $-1$ at $d \equiv 3 \pmod 4$. For $n = 0$ there are no divisors and the sum is $0$.
nodes.title: Divisor sum of the character modulo 4

nodes.summary: For a natural number $j$, the map $(a, b) \mapsto a + bi$ is a bijection from the set of integer pairs $(a, b)$ with $a^2 + b^2 = j$ to the set of Gaussian integers $z$ with norm $N(z) = j$; its inverse sends $z$ to the pair of its real and imaginary parts.
nodes.title: Sums of two squares as Gaussian norms

nodes.summary: For every natural number $j$, the representation number $r_2(j)$ equals the number of pairs $(a, b)$ of integers with $a^2 + b^2 = j$.
nodes.title: Two-square representation numbers count integer pairs

nodes.summary: Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, so $\chi_4(d)$ is $0$ for even $d$, $1$ for $d \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and $-1$ for $d \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.
